title: Correctness guardrail for INT8 path in CI (numerical drift checks + fallback criteria)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Goal
- Add an automated correctness guardrail for the INT8 inference path that catches numerical drift regressions early (presubmit where feasible + nightly), with explicit fallback criteria for disabling INT8 per model/GPU when we detect unacceptable drift.

Why
- We’re landing multiple INT8 kernel + scheduler changes during the FP8/INT8 sprint. Performance wins are not acceptable if we silently degrade outputs.
- We have at least one recent signal of customer-perceived latency regression on INT8 variants after runtime updates (see SUP-6193) and separate reports of output quality concerns on quantized paths (SUP-6194). Even if those are not purely INT8, we need hard guardrails.

Non-goals
- Full benchmark/eval suite (that remains in Applied ML pipelines). This is a CI guardrail focused on numerical stability and obvious correctness failures.
- Model-quality research or prompt set curation beyond a small representative prompt set.

Proposed guardrail (what we check)
1) Deterministic decode equivalence (primary)
- Run greedy decode (temperature=0, top_p=1) for N decode tokens using FP16 baseline and INT8 path.
- Metric: token match rate across the generated sequence (excluding the prompt), plus “first divergence position”.
- Threshold (initial): >= 97% token match for each prompt; if < 97% OR first divergence occurs within first 8 decoded tokens => FAIL.

2) Logit drift (secondary, more stable than token match for near-ties)
- For each decode step, compare FP16 vs INT8 logits on a fixed top-K set (K=20 by FP16 rank).
- Metric: mean absolute diff (MAD) + max abs diff across steps; also detect NaN/Inf.
- Threshold (initial): MAD <= 1e-2 and max abs diff <= 5e-2; any NaN/Inf => FAIL.

3) Sanity invariants
- No NaNs/Inf in activations/logits.
- No runtime fallback to FP16 unless explicitly allowed by the test configuration (we want to detect accidental “INT8 silently disabled”).
- Kernel-selection + quant-mode tags recorded in the test artifact (for triage).

Prompts / coverage (small but representative)
- Prompt set: 10 prompts total, split across:
  - short chat (prefill-light)
  - long-context chat (prefill-heavy, ~4k tokens input) — historically where we saw sensitivity
  - code completion
  - structured instruction following (JSON-ish output)
  - “edge” prompts with repetition / punctuation (tends to stress numerics)
- Models (CI set): one per top hosted family:
  - Llama-family (8B class)
  - Qwen-family (7B class)
  - Mistral-family (7B class)
- GPUs: presubmit on A100 (primary), nightly matrix expands to H100/H200 + L40S as capacity permits.

CI integration plan
A) Presubmit (required check only for relevant changes)
- Trigger condition: changes in runtime quantization codepaths / kernels / kernel auto-selection / scheduler policies touching quant mode.
- Runtime: target < 12 minutes on a single GPU runner.
- 1 run per model with 3 prompts (fast subset), N=32 decode tokens.

B) Nightly (full drift suite)
- Trigger: nightly scheduled job.
- Full prompt set + all CI models; more repetitions for stability (3 runs, take median for logit metrics; for token match use majority vote at each position).
- Artifacts uploaded in the standard benchmark/perf-canary format (include runtime commit, container digest, GPU clocks).

Fallback criteria (what we do on failure)
- Presubmit failure: block merge.
- Nightly failure:
  1) Page/notify #eng-runtime with artifact link and summary (model/GPU/commit, first divergence, drift stats).
  2) If failure reproduces twice within 24h on the same (model,GPU) pair: automatically apply a safe fallback in config for that pair before the next release train:
     - Prefer: disable INT8 for that model family on that GPU SKU via model registry perf profile override, OR
     - Restrict INT8 to known-safe shapes if the failure correlates to specific sequence-length / batch patterns.
  3) Add an allowlist entry only if we have a documented explanation and a remediation owner + due date.

Acceptance criteria
- A CI job exists that runs INT8 vs FP16 drift checks and reports:
  - token match rate + first divergence position
  - logit MAD + max abs diff (top-K)
  - NaN/Inf detection
  - metadata tags: model id, GPU SKU, runtime commit, quant mode, chosen kernel ids
- Path-based gating is enabled so unrelated PRs aren’t blocked.
- Results are stored as artifacts and linked from the CI run.
- Documented thresholds + initial allowlist policy live in repo docs (and linked from the sprint methodology).
- On failure, instructions are clear for triage + the fallback mechanism (disable INT8 per model/GPU) is explicitly defined.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Determinism: we must fix random seeds and force deterministic kernels where possible; if unavoidable nondeterminism remains, token-match should be treated as a heuristic and logit drift should be the main signal.
- Flake control: use pinned container digest + pinned driver/CUDA per perf-lab (ENG-24812). For nightly, record GPU clocks and enforce a warmup pass.

comments:
2025-10-01 — Sahana Iyer
Drafted a small drift harness using our existing generation test scaffolding: runs FP16 then INT8 with identical decode params and captures per-step logits for top-K comparison. Next: settle thresholds with Applied ML (Jonas/Priyanka) and confirm which models to include in presubmit vs nightly.

Open question: token-match rate is too sensitive on near-tie distributions; I’d like logit MAD/top-K to be the primary and token-match as secondary + divergence position for debugging.

2025-10-02 — Jonas Weber
Agree token-match can be noisy for near-ties, especially on code prompts. Suggest we:
- Treat NaN/Inf as hard fail.
- Use logit-based thresholds as the gate.
- Keep token divergence position purely for operator ergonomics.
For initial thresholds, MAD <= 1e-2 and max abs <= 5e-2 seems reasonable for INT8 if scaling is stable; we can loosen slightly on L40S if we see consistent borderline cases (but require a documented allowlist entry).

2025-10-03 — Sean Gallagher
Perf-lab GPU runner availability: presubmit can run on the shared A100 lane with ~15 min budget, but we need to keep it lean. Nightly can expand to H100 + L40S; H200 will be ready once the provisioning ticket clears. Please make sure the job records container digest and GPU clocks; we’ve seen false positives from background contention.

Also: prefer 1 warmup iteration before recording metrics.

2025-10-06 — Sahana Iyer
Implemented path-based gating: the check is required only when files under runtime/quant, runtime/kernels, runtime/scheduler/quant touched. Others get an informational nightly-only signal.

PR up: redwood#10627
- Adds quant_drift_check runner
- Adds thresholds + failure summary

Need review from Connor (policy) + Jonas (thresholds).

2) Clarify fallback criteria wording: disable INT8 per (model family, GPU SKU) rather than “global disable”, and require an owner + due date for any allowlist.

Once updated, OK to merge for runtime-1.18 cut.
